inspection_summary: Verified the frozen 874-line normalized source and inspected every line. The article builds an auxiliary family of completed multiple Dirichlet series, transports a known polar divisor through two functional equations to the point (s,w)=(1/2,3/4), computes and projects its residue back to the original cubic-moment series, and then converts that pole into a conditional x^(3/4) secondary term by contour shifting. Formula extraction is imperfect but the prose, transformations, propositions, and proof architecture remain recoverable.

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Frames quadratic Dirichlet moments, introduces the multiple-series encoding, states the conditional pole and secondary-term results, and explains their significance and dependencies.

sections_inspected.label: Symbols and notations

sections_inspected.label: Functional equations
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Constructs the completed two-variable family, states its two generating functional equations, and traces the unique candidate pole to (1/2,3/4).

accepted_units.title: Encode the cubic moment as a two-variable Dirichlet series
accepted_units.why_material: The discriminant exponent becomes a complex variable w, so moment asymptotics can be studied through the singularities of Z(s,w); this is the central representation change driving the paper.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the moment problem, conjectural polynomial degree, and the definition of the series; the displayed formulas are readable despite stray extraction glyphs.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on viewing a family average as coefficients of a Dirichlet series in the discriminant variable.

accepted_units.title: Möbius expansion transfers continuation from square-divisible auxiliary series
accepted_units.why_material: The expansion over r explains how controlled auxiliary series recover the desired squarefree family and why absolute convergence of that outer expansion sets the accessible w-region and the previous error exponent.
accepted_units.context_note: The definitions (1.4)-(1.6), the continuation region, and its consequence for the cubic moment are kept together.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the squarefree restriction being represented by a Möbius-weighted sum of series with r^2 dividing the index.

accepted_units.title: A transported pole predicts an exceptional cubic-moment term
accepted_units.why_material: The two conditional theorems connect a nonzero simple pole at w=3/4 to an x^(3/4) secondary term, state the necessary continuation and growth hypotheses, and distinguish the structural phenomenon from what remains analytically out of reach.
accepted_units.context_note: The immutable v1 span is already self-contained: it includes both theorem statements, the growth-condition discussion, the exceptional-term interpretation, and the proof roadmap.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the meromorphic generating-series representation; the explicit residue and gamma/Euler-product constants are formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Separate squarefree kernels and bad Euler factors
accepted_units.why_material: Factoring each integer into a squarefree kernel and square part, then separating Euler factors at a chosen modulus, supplies the bookkeeping needed to move between primitive characters, imprimitive indices, and completed L-functions.
accepted_units.context_note: The prose and definitions (2.1)-(2.5) are recoverable; individual symbols suffer minor font-extraction substitutions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on prime-local factorization and parity-sensitive archimedean gamma factors.

accepted_units.title: Package finite-prime corrections for residue transport
accepted_units.why_material: The B, A, E, and R factors compress the exceptional-prime algebra into multiplicative objects later recognized inside residue sums, enabling a global Euler-product computation rather than repeated casewise expansions.
accepted_units.context_note: This span is heavily formula-dependent; its structural role and named definitions are recoverable, but exact reuse requires checking the rendered source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strong dependence on exact Euler factors, character values, and superscript/subscript placement; scan verification is advisable for coefficients.

accepted_units.title: Choose correction polynomials so two summation orders satisfy reciprocal identities
accepted_units.why_material: The polynomials P and Q complete the coefficients so that summing first in d or n yields the same object; the resulting Z_M admits global meromorphic continuation and exposes its candidate polar lines.
accepted_units.context_note: Contains the defining reciprocity identity, the completed series, and the initial pole classification; exact polynomial formulas are extraction-sensitive but the construction is clear.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on a two-variable multiple Dirichlet series completed by finite Dirichlet polynomials at nonsquarefree and bad-prime data.

accepted_units.title: Functional-equation orbit carries the original pole to w=3/4
accepted_units.why_material: Two affine transformations of (s,w), arising respectively from the L-function functional equation and quadratic reciprocity, carry the simple pole at (1/4,1) through (3/4,1/4) to (1/2,3/4) and show that no other transformed original pole can account for that candidate.
accepted_units.context_note: The immutable v1 span contains both propositions and the full pole-orbit argument; no surrounding expansion is needed to understand the mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the completed Z_M family and on reading the two exact affine transformations; coefficient matrices in the displayed equations are formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.unit_type: residue propagation through first functional equation
accepted_units.title: Pull the w=1 residue across the first symmetry
accepted_units.why_material: Proposition 3 evaluates the residue on the first transformed polar line by inserting the known w=1 residue into the first functional equation and collapsing divisor sums into previously defined finite Euler factors.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof works out one congruence case and states that the remaining cases are analogous; the semantic mechanism is intact although exact case coefficients need rendered-formula checking.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on gamma-factor parity cases and multiplicative local corrections E and D.

accepted_units.unit_type: residue propagation through second functional equation
accepted_units.title: Move the residue onto the line w=(3-3s)/2
accepted_units.why_material: Combining the second functional equation with Proposition 3 produces an explicit residue on the polar line that contains (1/2,3/4), while the proof shows how a divisor sum factors into an A-factor and a small 2-adic correction.
accepted_units.context_note: The proposition, piecewise local factor, and representative b congruent to 1 mod 4 computation form one coherent derivation; other cases are explicitly omitted by the source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly depends on exact gamma ratios, congruence cases, and 2-adic Euler factors; use the source rendering for literal formulas.

accepted_units.title: Recover the original discriminant series by sign and mod-8 classes
accepted_units.why_material: Proposition 5 expresses Z as a fixed linear combination of auxiliary sign/parity series, making explicit how the prime 2 and the classification of fundamental discriminants mediate the return from Z_M-like objects to the original moment series.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof identifies the mechanism as a case split by sign and residue class modulo 8.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the local Euler factor at 2 and the classification of fundamental discriminants.

accepted_units.title: Remove square factors through a Möbius-weighted residue identity
accepted_units.why_material: Proposition 6 turns the assumed expansion over r into an exact expression for the desired residue in terms of residues of the M=2 completed family, preserving the squarefree constraint while exposing multiplicative factors.
accepted_units.context_note: The displayed identity has OCR symbol damage, but the Möbius-sieve structure and its derivation from (1.6) and the cited decomposition are clear.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on Möbius inversion, squarefree kernels, and character twists; exact summation indices require rendered-source verification.

accepted_units.title: Only the principal-character Euler product survives the limiting residue
accepted_units.why_material: The proof reduces all residue contributions to Euler products R(chi,chi',chi''), shows via orders of L- and zeta-factors that every contribution with a nontrivial character vanishes, and retains the principal-character term to obtain the explicit nonzero residue.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the decisive cancellation/nonvanishing mechanism rather than routine constant arithmetic; some character decorations are blurred but the selection argument is explicit in prose.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on Euler-product factorization and comparing pole orders at 1; the final numeric and gamma-factor constant is formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Convert the w=3/4 pole into an x^(3/4) secondary main term
accepted_units.why_material: Perron inversion, shifting from Re(w)>1 to Re(w)=sigma_0+epsilon, and balancing the vertical-growth and truncation errors show exactly how the order-seven pole at 1 yields xR_3(log x) while the simple pole at 3/4 yields the exceptional secondary term.
accepted_units.context_note: The argument is conditional on the stated boundary growth estimate and uses a sharp cutoff; its prose and exponent balancing are recoverable despite formula glyph noise.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on Mellin/Perron inversion, pole-to-asymptotic correspondence, and the chosen truncation height T.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Pole orbit to secondary asymptotic
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A functional-equation orbit can reveal a hidden polar contribution, but it becomes a genuine secondary term only after nonvanishing survives arithmetic projection and contour shifting is controlled.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This source proves the residue computation conditionally on continuation assumptions and derives the unweighted asymptotic only under a separate growth bound.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Auxiliary completion followed by arithmetic projection
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: One may enlarge a difficult squarefree family to a completed multivariable family with usable symmetries, perform analytic work there, and then return through congruence decomposition and Möbius sieving.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The construction is tailored to quadratic characters and its correction polynomials; no general transfer principle is established.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Local factors as a global selection rule
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Packaging congruence and bad-prime corrections multiplicatively makes the final residue a comparison of Euler-product pole orders, turning many elaborate intermediate terms into zero unless all characters are principal.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Exact coefficients and several case formulas are extraction-sensitive, and the paper explicitly computes only representative congruence cases in detail.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Analytic boundary quality controls observable moment precision
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The reach of meromorphic continuation and the vertical growth exponent jointly determine whether a transported pole can be separated from the contour error in an unweighted moment asymptotic.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The desired stronger growth estimate is suggested by symmetry and Phragmen-Lindelof reasoning but is not obtained here.
